claim_boundaries: These sources are benchmark, protocol, compliance, provenance, and governance inputs only.
These sources do not externally establish GMUT.
These sources do not externally establish Trinity Hybrid OS.
These sources do not externally establish Freed ID or Cosmic Bill.
These sources do not convert repo proposals into legal recognition, clinical clearance, or benchmark superiority.

inputs.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
inputs.title: Practices for Automated Benchmark Evaluations of Language Models
inputs.why_it_matters: Provides voluntary benchmark-evaluation practices for language models and AI agent systems across objective setting, benchmark selection, execution, analysis, and qualified reporting.
inputs.allowed_repo_use: Use as a benchmark-methodology and reporting-discipline comparator for bounded Trinity and Body evaluation language.
inputs.disallowed_repo_use: Do not cite as proof that repo benchmarks already satisfy NIST practices or that any repo system has externally established performance.

inputs.title: MLCommons Releases New MLPerf Inference v5.1 Benchmark Results
inputs.why_it_matters: Describes an open-source, peer-reviewed, architecture-neutral, representative, and reproducible benchmark suite with modern latency-sensitive and reasoning workloads.
inputs.allowed_repo_use: Use as external benchmark vocabulary for latency, throughput, reproducibility, and workload scoping.
inputs.disallowed_repo_use: Do not treat as a Trinity result, parity claim, or superiority claim without direct compliant submissions.

inputs.title: Transports
inputs.why_it_matters: Defines the standard MCP transport mechanisms, Streamable HTTP security requirements, session handling, and protocol-version behavior.
inputs.allowed_repo_use: Use as a protocol comparator for agent transport surfaces, origin validation, and session/header handling.
inputs.disallowed_repo_use: Do not present transport support as proof of production safety, autonomy maturity, or external establishment.

inputs.title: Sampling
inputs.why_it_matters: Defines standardized client-mediated model invocation, sampling capabilities, tool-enabled requests, and human-in-the-loop review expectations.
inputs.allowed_repo_use: Use as a protocol and safety-pattern input for bounded agent-tool interaction notes.
inputs.disallowed_repo_use: Do not treat sampling support as evidence of safe deployment, approved autonomy, or verified runtime control.

inputs.title: Verifiable Credentials Data Model v2.0
inputs.why_it_matters: Defines the issuer-holder-verifier credential model, normative document requirements, media types, and verification expectations for interoperable verifiable credentials and presentations.
inputs.allowed_repo_use: Use as the core credential and presentation semantics comparator for Freed ID alignment notes.
inputs.disallowed_repo_use: Do not treat format conformance or verifiability as proof of claim truth, trust-framework acceptance, or legal recognition.

inputs.title: OpenID for Verifiable Credential Issuance 1.0
inputs.why_it_matters: Defines the API and OAuth-based issuance flow for verifiable credentials, including credential offers, metadata, authorization details, and deferred issuance.
inputs.allowed_repo_use: Use as an issuance-flow comparator for wallet, issuer, and credential-delivery interoperability notes.
inputs.disallowed_repo_use: Do not treat alignment with the issuance protocol alone as proof of ecosystem trust, deployment readiness, or regulatory compliance.

inputs.title: OpenID for Verifiable Presentations 1.0
inputs.why_it_matters: Defines the OAuth-based protocol for requesting and presenting credentials, including verifier metadata and supported proof and format negotiation.
inputs.allowed_repo_use: Use as a presentation-flow comparator for verifier, wallet, and proof-negotiation notes.
inputs.disallowed_repo_use: Do not treat presentation-protocol support as proof of identity-assurance level, trust-framework acceptance, or legal validity.

inputs.title: Guidelines for providers of general-purpose AI models
inputs.why_it_matters: Clarifies scope, thresholds, exemptions, and enforcement timelines for provider obligations under the EU AI Act GPAI provisions.
inputs.allowed_repo_use: Use as a compliance-comparator input for scope, transparency, copyright, systemic-risk, and enforcement-timeline notes.
inputs.disallowed_repo_use: Do not present the guidelines as certification, a legal opinion for repo artifacts, or evidence that the repo already satisfies EU GPAI obligations.

inputs.title: General-Purpose AI Code of Practice now available
inputs.why_it_matters: Captures the voluntary transparency, copyright, and safety-security control structure that the Commission positions as a practical compliance tool for GPAI providers.
inputs.allowed_repo_use: Use as a control-matrix and disclosure-pattern comparator for bounded compliance notes.
inputs.disallowed_repo_use: Do not treat voluntary code alignment as legal approval, enforcement immunity, or proof that the repo is an in-scope GPAI provider.

inputs.publisher: Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity
inputs.title: Guidance for Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
inputs.why_it_matters: Shows how C2PA content credentials can provide tamper-evident provenance for datasets, software, models, and AI outputs in training and inference workflows.
inputs.allowed_repo_use: Use as a provenance and integrity comparator for dataset, model, artifact, and output lineage notes.
inputs.disallowed_repo_use: Do not equate provenance metadata with factual truth, model quality, policy legitimacy, or external establishment of repo claims.

inputs.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Device Software Functions: Lifecycle Management and Marketing Submission Recommendations
inputs.why_it_matters: Provides FDA lifecycle-risk and submission-documentation expectations for AI-enabled device software functions across the total product life cycle.
inputs.allowed_repo_use: Use as a wetware-health governance comparator for lifecycle documentation, safety-effectiveness evidence, and change-management expectations.
inputs.disallowed_repo_use: Do not treat this draft guidance as implementation approval, device clearance, or evidence that any repo artifact satisfies FDA requirements.

inputs.title: Ethics and governance of artificial intelligence for health
inputs.why_it_matters: Sets WHO's broad ethics, human-rights, accountability, and public-benefit governance frame for AI in health.
inputs.allowed_repo_use: Use as a health-governance comparator for ethics, accountability, and public-benefit framing in wetware-adjacent notes.
inputs.disallowed_repo_use: Do not treat WHO guidance as clinical authorization, regulatory approval, or evidence that repo systems are safe for health deployment.

inputs.title: Ethics and governance of artificial intelligence for health: Guidance on large multi-modal models
inputs.why_it_matters: Provides a current WHO governance lens for large multi-modal or general-purpose foundation models in health contexts.
inputs.allowed_repo_use: Use as a health-governance and model-risk comparator for wetware and clinical-adjacent notes.
inputs.disallowed_repo_use: Do not treat this guidance as proof that large multi-modal models are appropriate for repo uses or that repo artifacts satisfy WHO expectations.

inputs.title: Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence
inputs.why_it_matters: Provides a global normative ethics frame centered on proportionality, do no harm, human oversight, accountability, and rule-of-law-oriented governance.
inputs.allowed_repo_use: Use as a high-level governance comparator for rights, oversight, accountability, and harm-minimization language.
inputs.disallowed_repo_use: Do not treat the UNESCO recommendation as direct legal force, proof of policy adoption, or external establishment of repo governance claims.
